records.description_evidence: Assembly standards: not RFC\[10], on an EcoRI site at 3921, and not Type IIS / RFC 1000, on a SapI site at 177. RFC 1000 compatibility turns on BsaI and SapI alone, and there is no BsaI site. Both blocking sites are inherited from the lacZ and sfGFP reference parts, and neither crosses a junction, so the assembly introduces none of its own. The insert also carries three BbsI sites at 558, 2427 and 3693 and two BsmBI sites at 1538 and 2490, all inside sfGFP or lacZ; neither enzyme belongs to the standard, so neither affects the verdict.

cds_evidence.label: gfaspurple
cds_evidence.translation_reason: No source-provided translation qualifier in this API feature; no protein synthesized

records.description_evidence: GfasPurple is a protein-based chromoprotein engineered for stable coloration in synthetic biology systems. It is designed to serve as a cofactor-free purple biopigment that maintains color intensity under ambient light without requiring external cofactors. The protein exhibits high stability under elevated temperatures and oxidative/reductive conditions, maintaining its chromatic properties in challenging environments. These characteristics make GfasPurple suitable for visual reporting applications in biosensing and as a durable colorant for industrial biotechnology. We cloned the *gfaspurple* into the pET-28a(+) vector to expand the functional characterization of the existing part BBa\_K5357010 through comprehensive analysis of its thermal resistance and redox tolerance

records.description_evidence: This TyrBm expression device is driven by the T7 promoter and expresses Tyrosinase from *Bacillus megaterium* (TyrBm). TyrBm converts L-Tyrosine into L-DOPA, then transforms L-DOPA into Dopaquinone and ultimately forms eumelanin through oxidation, providing a strategy for the formation of natural black pigments.
